effect: Turns on the debug mode left in the game: a scene select, five debug tools and a Select pause
note: One ROM byte, $80:8077 (file offset $8077: 00 → 01), is the switch; the game reads it at $C0:8206, $C0:8493, $C0:8FF1 and $C0:90F0. Mesen's cheat engine, same inputs and frame: without the code the boot carries on to the JBA logo, with it the scene select opens. DF65-7FAD, the same byte in bank $C0, does not work: the reads go through bank $80. The same debug flag is known through a Pro Action Replay code.

effect: トライ ∞: a failed stage is retried until you clear it
note: $0D85 is the tries setting, 0-2 for 1-3 tries and 3 for ∞, a value the Option screen only offers once your best rank is 6 or higher. Mesen's cheat engine: the Option screen read トライ ∞ at once. The retry loop itself ($C2:84E3) was read, not played.

effect: The Option screen's トライ setting gains its hidden fourth value, ∞
note: $0D83 is the best rank reached. Written in Mesen: Right on トライ cycled 2 → 3 → ∞ → 1; with $0D83 = 0 it cycled 2 → 3 → 1. The picture is the second press of Right, 1 against ∞.

code: Reach rank 6, ハイパービーダー
effect: トライ on the Option screen can be set to ∞, unlimited tries on each stage
note: The Option screen lets the tries setting reach 3 (∞) only when the best-rank byte $0D83 is 6 or more ($C2:B020, $C2:B04A); the rank is raised at $C1:B166 and saved. Rank 6 is ハイパービーダー: a total of 9250 or more over the 100 stages' best scores (see the certificate card).

effect: New title music, a bronze Bomberman on the title, and a SPECIAL entry on the menu
note: Every 10-stage Normal level ends with a certificate. Its rank comes from the total of the file's best scores on all 100 stages, each at most 100: 3000, 6000, 8000, 8500, 9000, 9250, 9500, 9800 and 10000 are ranks 1 to 9 ($C1:BB22, table $C1:BB4A). The best rank over all files is saved ($30:628D) and the title and menu read it: at rank 4 (8500) the title plays BGM 16 instead of 01, the Bomberman turns bronze, and SPECIAL appears after OPTION. Shown by writing the save and resetting, and the edge by writing the stage scores before a certificate: 8499 gave rank 3, 8500 rank 4. GameFAQs lists the music and Special for over 800 on each of the 10 levels; that is 8000 in all, rank 3, which changes nothing. The music number was logged, not listened to. Picture: the certificates for 8499 and 8500.

effect: SURVIVAL joins the menu and the title Bomberman turns silver, then gets a red ball, then turns gold
note: Rank 5 (9000): silver Bomberman with a green ball and SURVIVAL after SPECIAL. Rank 6 (9250): a red ball. Rank 9 (10000, every stage at 100): a gold Bomberman, the certificate マスター攻略王. Nothing checks that every stage was cleared, only the total, so about 90 stages at full score are needed. A certificate with all 100 scores written at 100 saved rank 9, and after a reset the title showed the gold Bomberman with SPECIAL and SURVIVAL on the menu. GameFAQs gives silver, Special and Survival for clearing all 100 levels and gold for 10000. Picture: ranks 6 and 9.

effect: A fourth entry, ????, under NEW GAME: ten 10-stage levels with their own scores and a save record of their own
note: It appears when the count of certificates ever awarded ($30:6347, across all files) reaches 100. It opens a B-Daman select, a level select with ten level scores, then a 10-stage level, saved to a fourth record. How it differs from Normal was not worked out. Shown by writing the count. Picture: the menu with ????, and its level select.

code: Clear 100 stages in a row in Survival
effect: The menu's cursor ball turns gold
note: Survival plays stages 1 to 100 in order with one try each and keeps the best run ($30:6346). At 100 the end screen reads マスター攻略王, "すごいぞっ！キミも攻略王だっ！おめでとう！", and the menu cursor becomes a gold ball. Shown by writing the count; the end screen was reached by jumping to it, not by playing 100 stages.

code: DF65-4FAD, then Start + Select on the Hudson logo, then Start + Select again
effect: Scene select: STAGE xx and the name of every scene in the game, 100 normal stages included
note: Start + Select on the Hudson logo sets $1F5A (the game as sold does this too, but nothing reads it without the debug byte). After that, Start + Select held in any scene opens the list ($83:8000). A +1, B -1, X +$10, Y -$10, Start runs the scene, L and R open two of the tools; Start + Select inside a scene comes back. Names are in half-width kana (table $83:B19B).

effect: BOMB ENTRY EDIT: a stage's bomb list, one row a bomb
note: $83:A0AC. Rows like 01 00 0030 FE50 08 under NO = 00, COUNT = 07.

effect: MOVE TYPE EDIT: the bombs' movement scripts
DEBUG MODE DATA SET: eight flag bytes as bits and 32 data words
note: $83:8571. FLAG0-7 are $1F4E-$1F55 and DATAnn the word at $1F56 + 2n. The D-pad moves, A raises and B lowers a cell, Start leaves. FLAG0 bit 0 adds a MOVE TYPE readout to the stage editor; FLAG2 bit 0 swaps the Battle arena for Battle Stage 2.

effect: SOUND TEST: BGM NO and SE NO
note: $83:828B. The Option screen has its own BGM and SE test.

effect: EXPLOSIOIN PARAM. SET (sic): the size and timing of small, middle and large blasts
note: $83:844B. Rows INIT, END, ADD, KEEP, SUB, HOLD and H ADD.

effect: The stage editor shows a MOVE TYPE nn readout
note: FLAG0 of the debug data page, read when EDIT starts ($C2:8F94). Written to RAM in Mesen, not through the cheat engine.

effect: A second battle arena, バトル ステージ ソノ2, that the game never picks
note: Battle loads scene $17 instead of $13 only when bit 0 of $1F50 is set ($C1:D9A9, $C1:F4BF, $C2:DCF1), and nothing but the debug data page writes that byte: the rules screen changed none of the flag bytes with every row toggled. The arena was seen through the scene select; the flag wasn't watched working in a real Battle. Picture: the normal arena and Battle Stage 2.

effect: The game boots into an empty wooden stage with nothing to hit
note: On a PAL console the boot stores scene $00 ($C0:80E8), its only use. Seen with Mesen's region set to PAL.

effect: "You can not use a mouse with this game."
note: Scene $9C, shown after the JBA logo. Seen with a mouse in port 2.

effect: Sound driver credits that are never shown
note: File $4D58A: SFX SOUND DRIVER Ver 2.32 / 1993-96 Hudson Soft / Program : LU.Iwabuchi / Driver : Kazumi-TYPE / Note :
